methods.label: Check the partition and calculate conditionally
methods.explanation:
First check whether the drawing shows the partition described in the question.

[Figure 1](figures/1998_AMC_12_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

There are four segments from the center to the boundary: one to each left corner, one to a point on the top side, and one to a point on the right side. They divide the square into four regions, including two triangles. This differs from the stated three regions consisting of two trapezoids and a pentagon.

There is also an area contradiction. The triangle along the left side has base \(1\). Since its third vertex is the square's center, its perpendicular height is \(\frac12\). Its area is therefore
\[
\frac12\cdot1\cdot\frac12=\frac14.
\]
But a unit square has area \(1\), so three equal-area regions would each have area \(\frac13\). Thus the drawing cannot satisfy the stated partition, and no value of \(x\) makes all the displayed conditions consistent.

For a conditional calculation, assume the figure is corrected to show three equal-area regions, with each trapezoid having parallel sides \(x\) and \(\frac12\), separated by a perpendicular height of \(\frac12\). These are assumptions about a corrected figure. The trapezoid-area formula then gives
\[
\frac12\left(x+\frac12\right)\frac12=\frac13.
\]
Multiplying by \(4\) and subtracting \(\frac12\), we obtain
\[
x=\frac43-\frac12=\frac56.
\]
This satisfies \(\frac12<x<1\), and its trapezoid area is \(\frac13\). Hence \(\boxed{\frac56}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\), is the answer under that correction. The displayed item itself remains inconsistent.
